sessions.title: Gut-Health Breakfast: Elevating IQ and Happiness through Gut Health
sessions.who: Masaomi Sakata (Koji Ouji) with the Obaachan Shokudo team · 60 servings, first come first served
sessions.description:
Masaomi Sakata introduces his approach to gut health through food education and conscious choices about what we eat. Rather than focusing only on adding products or supplements, he asks participants to consider what they might leave out of their everyday diets.

The session explores his philosophy of intentional subtraction: paying attention to unnecessary additives, highly processed foods, and the habits that shape daily eating. He also discusses how he connects food choices with sensory awareness and mental clarity. The emphasis is on reconsidering familiar routines and developing a more intentional relationship with food. Participants are invited to reflect on what conscious eating means in their own lives.

sessions.title: Opening: Chikuzen Hakata Koma
sessions.who: Chikushi Shuraku III · 480 years of spinning-top performance · Welcome MC: Nikoleta Kouli
sessions.description:
Experience Chikuzen Hakata Koma, a traditional spinning-top performance with a history of 480 years. Recognized as an intangible cultural property of Fukuoka Prefecture, this art brings together craftsmanship, physical skill, and techniques developed through years of practice.

Chikushi Shuraku III presents an opportunity to encounter Japanese cultural history through live performance rather than explanation alone. The tradition has been performed for imperial and royal audiences and in countries around the world. Its movements are accomplished through the performer’s technique, without hidden mechanisms. Watching the tops in motion offers a direct encounter with the patience, precision, and accumulated knowledge behind this Fukuoka performing art.

sessions.title: Keynote 1: Why We Came, Why We Stayed, and What Comes Next
sessions.who: Nick Szasz (FUKUOKA NOW) with Douglas Weber, Jean-Pierre Villeneuve and Micaela Anne
sessions.description:
What makes someone choose Fukuoka and build a life here? Fukuoka Now founder Nick Szasz brings together Douglas Weber, Jean-Pierre Villeneuve, and Micaela Anne to discuss the decisions and experiences that made a temporary stay become something lasting.

Douglas moved from product design at Apple to creating coffee equipment in Itoshima. Jean-Pierre built a karaoke technology business after arriving for what was meant to be a short visit. Micaela first came as an exchange student and now shares everyday life in Japan with an international audience. Their conversation explores why they arrived, what persuaded them to stay, and how they contribute to the place they now call home.

sessions.title: Keynote 2: Matcha Crisis
sessions.who: Yumi Imamura, Tea Farmers and Distributors
sessions.description:
Yumi Imamura leads a conversation about the current matcha boom and what it means for Japanese tea. The discussion begins with Matcha Crisis, then turns to Matcha in the Light: the possibilities that growing interest in matcha has created for Yame tea and Yame City in Fukuoka.

The closing theme, Matcha Bloom, asks what kind of future people want to create through Japanese tea. Yumi brings her perspective as a Japanese tea instructor who grew up in a tea-selling family and now shares tea culture in Japan and overseas. Her work includes mobile tea-room experiences that connect tea with time and place.

sessions.title: Destination Pitches (3 mins)
sessions.who: Local Craftsmen, Nagasaki City, Goto City, Hirado City, Yame City, Buzen City, Koga City, Hyuga City, Tour de Kyushu, Chiang Mai, Taiwan Digital Fest, SDEC (Sarawak Digital Economy Corporation), Co-Lab HAKUBA

sessions.title: Lunch Buffet + Sponsor Booth Time in the Garden
Where can we build something that matters?
sessions.who: Jacquie Wortley × Ryu Fujii + local destinations
sessions.description:
Jacquie Wortley and Ryu Fujii lead the launch session for Fukuoka Builders Coliving and its co-creation project. Together with local community managers, they explore practical challenges and opportunities in regional Japan, asking how people arriving from outside can help build something meaningful in each place.

The conversation introduces three regional contexts: Yame’s matcha and artisan heritage, Koga’s shopping streets and community revival, and Buzen’s natural landscapes and resources for mindful living. Jacquie brings experience in UX research and sustainable innovation; Ryu connects experimental communities with local projects. The session places local people and the specific character of each region at the center of potential collaboration.

sessions.title: Speak Before You're Ready
sessions.description:
Multilingual Matt leads a practical workshop on language learning as a way to connect, rather than a test of perfection. The focus is on finding the confidence to start conversations, communicate before feeling fully prepared, and respond to mistakes without losing the connection with another person.

Matt brings humor, storytelling, and practical language-learning advice from his experience studying and speaking multiple languages. His work explores the awkward, human side of communicating across borders, treating language as a practice in courage and humility. The session invites participants to think less about flawless performance and more about the relationships that become possible when they are willing to speak.

sessions.title: Become Yourself Here: Japan as the Place You Discover Who You Really Are
sessions.who: Kiki Fukai (Krossing) + immigration specialist Ellie Yamatsu
sessions.description:
What changes when visiting Japan becomes building a life here? Kiki Fukai explores long-term living as a process of self-discovery, looking at how cultural differences, everyday challenges, and unfamiliar expectations can reveal personal values and strengths.

The session connects these reflections with personal branding: how a person’s experience of Japan can become part of an authentic story rather than simply a record of travel. It also includes an overview of visa pathways with an immigration specialist, considering how different options relate to individual goals and longer-term plans. Participants can reflect on both the personal meaning and practical planning involved in moving from wanting to live in Japan to building a life here.

sessions.title: You Can't Outrun Your Life: How to Use Travel as a Catalyst for Reinvention
sessions.description:
Travel can change a setting without resolving the questions a person carries into it. Jessica Hagmaier shares what she learned after leaving the United States in 2024 to reset and rebuild her life, only to discover that distance did not remove familiar patterns and expectations.

Her session follows the uneven process of questioning a life that no longer worked and rebuilding around freedom, autonomy, and what mattered to her. Drawing on her experience as a creative strategist, writer, and speaker, Jessica considers how setbacks and intentional decisions can create room for change. The conversation offers a grounded look at reinvention, without presenting travel as an escape or waiting for perfect circumstances to begin.

sessions.title: CHATEA Workshop
SME Takeover Lab: How to Acquire a Small Business — Tools, Process & Win-Win Thinking
sessions.description:
Starting a business is not the only route to entrepreneurship. Stella Schneider explores acquiring an existing small or medium-sized business, where customers, operations, and cash flow are already in place.

Drawing on her experience as a German business strategist and founder of Business Wege, she introduces five phases of a business takeover. Participants consider what to look for, which questions to ask, and how to structure an agreement that works for both buyer and seller. The session connects succession challenges faced by business owners with opportunities for people seeking a practical route into ownership. Tools and frameworks from the German SME market provide a starting point for evaluating whether acquisition fits individual goals.

sessions.title: Content Strategy for Small Businesses
sessions.description:
Content strategy does not have to mean posting every day. Daycia shares an approach for small-business owners working with limited time and without an agency budget, drawing on her experience at Dentsu and P&G and on building the Daylightful media brand.

The session focuses on choosing content pillars that fit a business, developing a realistic publishing plan, and understanding the difference between content that attracts likes and content that brings clients. Rather than treating a larger following as the goal, participants consider how content can support their brand and business priorities. The emphasis is on a manageable framework for deciding what to create and why it matters.

sessions.title: CHATEA Workshop (continued)
YEN TO EN: Turning Money Back into Connection
sessions.who: Ryotaro Sakurai × Kazuhiro Arai (eumo) × Kotaro Motojima × Kiyoko Mitsui (KIBOTCHA)
sessions.description:
What does wealth mean when the conversation moves beyond earning money? Ryotaro Sakurai facilitates a discussion about connection, reciprocity, and forms of value rooted in Japanese perspectives on community.

The panel brings together Kazuhiro Arai of eumo, lawyer Kotaro Motojima, and Kiyoko Mitsui of KIBOTCHA. Their work spans empathy-based economic ideas, support for a circular society, and a place developed through post-disaster recovery. Using the relationship between yen, money, and en, human connection, they explore how resources and relationships can circulate together. The session invites participants to reconsider what they accumulate, what they share, and how a sense of richness can emerge through relationships rather than financial measures alone.

sessions.title: Breaking Conceptions: From Nomadic Couple to Nomadic Family
sessions.description:
After six years of traveling as a couple, Yarden Avirav and Roza Gavrilov became parents and began reconsidering assumptions about freedom, home, relationships, and themselves. They share what happened when a life organized around movement had to make room for a baby.

The session compares the ideas they held before parenthood with the reality they encountered. Some expectations proved wrong; others became more complicated. Alongside meaningful moments, they discuss exhaustion, frustration, changes in identity, and pressures on their relationship. This is not a claim that traveling with a baby is easy. It is a conversation about adapting a life you love when the people and responsibilities within it change.

sessions.title: Latino Dance: Bachata for Everyone
sessions.description:
Join Nika Rey for a bachata workshop introducing basic movements for both leaders and followers. The session combines explanation and practice, with attention to body movement, musicality, and connection.

Nika is an international dance instructor and event organizer whose work encourages people to move with music. This workshop offers a chance to explore the relationship between rhythm, movement, and dancing with another person through the foundations of bachata.

sessions.title: The "Death" of Digital Nomads — Zen, Impermanence, and Living in the Moment
sessions.description: Digital nomads live by constantly leaving — familiar cities, close friends, old identities. In a sense, we experience repeated "small deaths." This session explores Buddhist and Zen views on death, impermanence, and rebirth, and how they resonate with the nomadic life. We'll look at reincarnation, karma, and the Zen idea of the "Great Death" — completely letting go of the ego so that a freer self can be reborn. Drawing on the landscape of Katsuura and Nachi Falls, we'll reflect on what it means to live fully in this very moment. You'll leave with a gentler, more grounded way of seeing change, loss, and the freedom found in letting go.

sessions.title: Build Wealth. Find Your Purpose. Design a Life You Don't Need to Retire From.
sessions.description:
Diego Taira shares his journey from nearly two decades in Japan’s corporate world to financial independence at 40 and a life organized around purpose. This interactive workshop asks what freedom means beyond the idea of early retirement.

Through reflection, practical ideas, and conversation, participants explore how they want to spend their time, what they want their work to support, and the contribution they hope to make. The session connects questions of wealth with personal ikigai rather than treating money as an isolated goal. It is intended for entrepreneurs, corporate leaders, and anyone reconsidering a next chapter, offering space to identify priorities and consider practical first steps toward a more intentional life.

sessions.title: Ask a Digital Nomad: Open Roundtables with JDNA
sessions.who: Moe Nakano × Vitto Christaldi (Japan Digital Nomad Association) · runs 10:30-12:15
sessions.description:
The Garden becomes a space for open roundtable conversations between digital nomads and people working in Japanese regions. Facilitated by Moe Nakano, Vitto Christaldi, and the Japan Digital Nomad Association, the session connects visitors with regional operators, city officers, educators, founders, and students.

Small-group rounds explore digital nomadism in relation to tourism, startups, education, and nature, with support for conversation in Japanese and English. Questions collected in advance help participants move directly into the issues they want to discuss. Japanese participants can ask how nomads choose places and what makes them stay; visiting Co-Creators can hear what local communities are trying to build. The format prioritizes direct conversation rather than slides or a keynote.

sessions.title: IKIGAI MANIFESTATION: How to Turn Your Ikigai into an Extraordinary Life — The 5-Step Formula to Live the Life You Truly Want
sessions.description:
Akira Iguchi introduces his Ikigai Manifestation Method, connecting personal purpose with practical action. He describes manifestation as a process in which action changes results and those results can change beliefs about what is possible.

The session follows five steps: Ikigai, Gift, Purpose, Monetization, and Impact and Scaling. Participants are invited to identify something they currently consider impossible and apply the 1mm Rule: a small action within 24 hours, shared with one witness. Other exercises explore an ikigai hypothesis, learning from a role model, and a year-end Kaizen review. Drawing on his experience building businesses and writing books, Akira considers how individual strengths can become meaningful work and how that contribution might grow.
sessions.update_note: Updated session details. Moved from 11:30–12:15 to 10:30–11:15 on October 2 (JST).

sessions.title: Align and Connect with Your Ikigai Through Soul
sessions.description:
Roland Tokko brings stories, music, singing, and guided visualization into a shared circle focused on ikigai. Participants are invited to connect with their own sense of purpose while also making space for connection with the people around them.

A speaker, facilitator, and singer-songwriter from Estonia, Roland combines spoken reflection with live musical and guided experiences. His approach explores leadership through listening to an inner sense of direction, rather than relying only on external expectations. The session offers a different mode of participation from a conventional talk: an opportunity to reflect, listen, sing, and consider the vision participants want to bring into their lives and work.

sessions.title: Ask a Digital Nomad (continued)
Lunch Buffet
Wakachiai: From Everyday Talk to Deep Connection
sessions.description:
Mikiko and Hidehiko Sudo explore why people who care about each other can still become caught in distance and misunderstanding. Drawing on patterns they experienced in their own marriage, they use a simple map to show how one person’s pursuit of connection can meet another’s withdrawal.

Participants then experience Wakachiai, a heart-sharing practice that moves from everyday conversation into feelings and the stories behind reactions. The workshop involves sharing, receiving, and listening without interrupting, offering advice, or trying to fix another person. It offers a first step participants can try with a partner, friend, or colleague, considering how small, regular conversations can help build trust and support co-creation.

sessions.title: Travel Smarter, Work Safer: Everyday Security for Digital Nomads
sessions.description:
Working while traveling creates everyday security decisions, from connecting to public Wi-Fi to handling client information or responding to urgent messages. Adam Curnow, founder of KarasuSec, introduces a practical approach to recognizing and managing these risks without relying on technical jargon.

Participants use a four-part routine—See it, Size it, Secure it, Review it—to assess a travel-and-work scenario and develop a personal security plan. The session covers protecting accounts and devices, keeping backups and recovery options ready, and identifying useful contacts before a problem occurs. It also considers how to respond when something goes wrong, limit the damage, and use that experience to improve preparations for the next trip.

sessions.title: Why Being Yourself Is Your Superpower
sessions.description:
Most of us spend our lives performing for others: chasing approval, likes, or money, and hiding the parts of ourselves we think people won't accept. It's exhausting, and I want us to challenge that. 

I used to create content for views and money, and it felt like work. When I started doing it for myself, everything changed. I connected deeper and learned to feel free to be silly. 

In this conversational workshop, we'll explore together:
• What changes when we act for ourselves instead of for approval
• How to show up on camera as the real you in a digital world
• How to speak to an audience and truly connect, whether it's one person or thousands

sessions.title: Peace: One Conversation at a Time
sessions.who: Oren Chazan × Yeji Cheon × Cihan Boz
sessions.description:
Oren Chazan, Yeji Cheon, and Cihan Boz introduce a conversation-centered strand of the program that gives people space to listen and be heard. The emphasis is on practicing attention so that another person feels genuinely met, rather than discussing connection only as an idea.

Their wider approach includes small circles and opportunities to make sense of experiences as the festival unfolds. Within a busy schedule of talks, tours, and social events, the aim is to create room to process what participants are encountering. Oren brings experience in coliving and Nonviolent Communication. The session offers an introduction to a slower, more deliberate form of conversation and its place in community life.

sessions.title: The Power of a Smile: Creating Connection and Joy Within and Around You
sessions.description:
Carlyn Shaw explores two sides of a smile: the expression that opens a connection with someone else and the choice to meet an unexpected turn in life with a different perspective. She draws on her own experience of choosing to smile again after losing her front teeth.

This interactive session considers how everyday choices, curiosity, and a willingness to be present can influence relationships and opportunities. Carlyn connects these ideas with her long-held belief that people create possibilities. Rather than treating a smile as a superficial gesture, the conversation looks at what it can mean in work, personal life, and encounters with strangers, including moments when circumstances are not what we hoped for.

sessions.title: HEARIM: Building Trust Across Cultures at Work
sessions.description:
Working across cultures involves more than sharing a language. Expectations about timing, hierarchy, responsibility, silence, and communication can differ even when everyone understands the words being spoken.

Tressia H. Lee introduces HEARIM, a Korean-inspired framework for recognizing these unspoken expectations and building trust. Drawing on more than 14 years of experience with Korean and global teams, she shares examples of how small communication choices affect collaboration and professional relationships. Participants consider how to notice assumptions, express expectations more clearly, and use the framework with clients, colleagues, partners, and international communities. The focus is on practical choices that can support cross-cultural work and everyday professional communication.

sessions.title: Beneath Ikigai & Zen: Discovering the Hidden Worldview of Japan, and Your Own
sessions.description:
Ikigai and Zen are widely recognized, but what lies beneath them? Sanae Akima explores the worldview that has shaped aspects of Japanese culture, including relationships with nature and other people, harmony, purpose, and ma—the space in between.

A short experiential exercise invites participants to notice automatic reactions to difference, uncertainty, and unfamiliar perspectives. From there, the session examines the often invisible assumptions that influence what people regard as normal, right, or possible. Japan becomes a mirror for looking at one’s own worldview rather than simply a subject to learn about. Participants consider how noticing these patterns can make room for greater curiosity and more intentional choices in everyday life.

sessions.title: Beyond Social Media: Grow a Business Through Relationships, Trust and Community
sessions.description:
Lawrence Tuazon shares how relationships, trust, referrals, partnerships, and community helped him grow his coaching and publishing businesses without relying heavily on social media, websites, or paid advertising.

The session examines what relationship-driven business development looks like in practice: building trust before asking for a sale, offering value without expecting an immediate return, and allowing conversations to develop into collaborations and referrals. Lawrence draws on lessons from his own entrepreneurial experience to consider how these connections can support long-term growth. Participants are invited to shift attention from collecting followers toward developing relationships with people and communities, and to think about how that approach could fit their own work.

sessions.title: Anywhere, But Where?
sessions.description:
If work can happen anywhere, how do you choose where to live, and how do you begin to belong after arriving? This participatory workshop considers digital nomadism through the lens of ikigai, looking beyond what mobility offers an individual.

The discussion explores how a visitor’s presence can matter to the places they choose, as well as how those places support the life they hope to build. East Asia provides the context for examining changing relationships between local communities, remote workers, long-stay visitors, and people who maintain connections with more than one place. Participants are invited to reflect on the relationship between choosing a destination and finding a meaningful place within it.

sessions.title: Rain Won't Stop You, Wind Won't Stop You: Live Music, Picture Books and Miyazawa Kenji in Two Languages
sessions.who: Arthur Binard × Visions (Miki Tsukamoto, Kiyoshi Mamura) · 90 min
sessions.description:
Arthur Binard and Visions bring literature, picture-book imagery, and live music together in a performance centered on the work of Miyazawa Kenji. Binard’s English translations and spoken reflections are accompanied by piano, bass, and percussion from Miki Tsukamoto and Kiyoshi Mamura.

Images from picture-book work illustrated by Koji Yamamura add a visual dimension to the words and music. Binard’s commentary draws on Japanese history, landscapes, and language, combining close attention to meaning with humor. The performance offers an opportunity to encounter familiar and unfamiliar words through more than one language and art form, considering how translation, illustration, and musical interpretation can open different ways of experiencing a literary work.

sessions.title: What Keeps a Community Alive? From Shared Spaces to Shared Purpose
sessions.who: Marco Traina (BeetCommunity · Italia Nomad Fest) · 90 min
sessions.description:
Sharing a building does not automatically create a community. Marco Traina draws on BeetCommunity, Italia Nomad Fest, and COFO – Coliving Founders to explore the relationships and practices that turn shared space into a place of belonging.

Using examples of successes and failures, he examines movement from guest to participant, contributor, and community member. The session connects trust, shared experiences, and purpose with sustainability, the circular economy, and the sharing of resources and knowledge. It also introduces temporary citizenship: participating in and taking responsibility for a place rather than experiencing it only as a visitor. A short video brings in perspectives from coliving founders in different countries on what keeps a community alive.

sessions.title: A Conscious Pause: Closing Meditation at the Water's Edge
sessions.description:
After two days of ideas, conversations, and new connections, Freeman Fung guides a pause to reflect on what participants want to carry forward. This integration session focuses on making room for experience rather than adding more information.

Through self-reflection and meditation outdoors, Freeman invites participants to turn their attention inward and connect the Academy’s activities with their own sense of purpose. The group slows down to consider what has resonated and how those experiences might inform life beyond the event. The session is open to people without meditation experience. Participants may bring a journal if they have one, using the time to gather their thoughts before the conversations and experiences still ahead in Fukuoka.

speakers.session: SME Takeover Lab: How to Acquire a Small Business — Tools, Process & Win-Win Thinking
speakers.bio:
Stella Schneider is a German business strategist, solopreneur, and founder of Business Wege — with more than 9 years of experience helping founders and entrepreneurs find their right business model and path forward.

She's known for cutting through complexity: her framework covers everything from freelancing and solopreneurship to startups, SMEs, and Entrepreneurship Through Acquisition (ETA). At Nomad Summit Chiang Mai 2026, she walked a room full of digital nomads through the 5 business models that actually work for location-independent life — grounded in radical self-awareness before strategy.

At CoLive Fukuoka, she's going deeper: into the practical process of acquiring an existing SME — with direct tools from the German market and a Win-Win mindset for buyers and sellers alike.

speakers.name: Daycia
speakers.session: Content Strategy for Small Businesses
speakers.bio: Daycia created Daylightful, a media brand focused on human connection, intentional travel, and slow cultural immersion. Previously, she worked on content and campaign strategy at Dentsu and P&G. She now shares practical content strategies with small-business owners.

speakers.name: Yarden Avirav & Roza Gavrilov
speakers.session: Breaking Conceptions: From Nomadic Couple to Nomadic Family
speakers.bio: Yarden and Roza are the couple behind NomadsTwoGo. After years of living and working as digital nomads, becoming parents in 2025 changed how they think about travel, freedom, and home. They share their ongoing experience of finding a nomadic lifestyle that works for a family.

speakers.name: Nika Rey
speakers.session: Latino Dance: Bachata for Everyone
speakers.bio: Nika is an international dance instructor and event organizer who encourages people to move, connect, and enjoy music through dance.

speakers.name: Diego Taira
speakers.session: Build Wealth. Find Your Purpose. Design a Life You Don't Need to Retire From.
speakers.bio: Diego is the co-founder and CEO of Wealth Angels.

speakers.name: Roland Tokko
speakers.session: Align and Connect with Your Ikigai Through Soul
speakers.bio: Roland is an Estonian speaker, facilitator, and singer-songwriter, and co-founder of Becoming International. He combines speaking, live music, singing, and guided experiences to help people explore purpose and leadership in their own lives.

speakers.name: Adam Curnow
speakers.session: Travel Smarter, Work Safer: Everyday Security for Digital Nomads
speakers.bio: Adam founded KarasuSec and works in IT and cybersecurity. A digital nomad himself, he focuses on making security understandable and practical for people who work from anywhere.

speakers.name: Oren Chazan
speakers.session: Peace: One Conversation at a Time
speakers.bio: Oren co-owns Montino Coliving and works as an advertising consultant and business coach. Trained in Nonviolent Communication and related practices, he creates coliving and conversation experiences that encourage connection, community, and a more peaceful way of living.

speakers.name: Yeji Cheon
speakers.session: Peace: One Conversation at a Time
speakers.bio: Yeji founded Seoul Nooks, an intentional coliving and coworking community. Her work connects local Asian cultures with global nomad communities, using workshops and conversations to explore cultural differences, diversity, and how people live together.

speakers.name: Cihan Boz
speakers.session: Peace: One Conversation at a Time

speakers.name: Carlyn Shaw
speakers.session: The Power of a Smile: Creating Connection and Joy Within and Around You
speakers.bio: Carlyn is a speaker, writer, and creator of the Whoever Smiles First Wins movement and Live In Joy community. Through travel and everyday encounters, she encourages people to trust themselves, build connections, and make room for joy.

speakers.name: Tressia H. Lee
speakers.session: HEARIM: Building Trust Across Cultures at Work
speakers.bio: Tressia is a global marketing and Korean cultural strategist from Seoul. She created HEARIM, a Korean-informed communication framework for understanding unspoken expectations and building trust across cultures. Her background spans marketing, localization, education, and cultural strategy, alongside a remote-working career that began in 2014.

speakers.name: Lawrence Tuazon
speakers.session: Beyond Social Media: Grow a Business Through Relationships, Trust and Community
speakers.bio: Lawrence is an author, speaker, coach, and co-founder of Be Extraordinary Publishing. He helps people turn their experiences into meaningful work and grow businesses through relationships, partnerships, referrals, and community.

speakers.name: Rei Lee
speakers.session: Anywhere, But Where?
speakers.bio: Rei founded LocalNomad and explores the future of work, play, and belonging in legacy cities.

speakers.name: Marco Traina
speakers.session: What Keeps a Community Alive? From Shared Spaces to Shared Purpose
speakers.bio: Marco is an entrepreneur and community builder who founded BeetCommunity in Palermo and Italia Nomad Fest. He also co-founded COFO – Coliving Founders. His work connects remote workers and local residents, encouraging visitors to participate in local life and contribute to the communities that host them.

speakers.name: Freeman Fung
speakers.session: A Conscious Pause: Closing Meditation at the Water's Edge
speakers.bio: Freeman is a speaker, author, mindset coach, and meditation facilitator. He founded Travel To Transform and combines personal development with travel and conscious global citizenship. His work encourages people to cultivate presence, self-understanding, and meaningful connections.

speakers.name: Arthur Binard
speakers.session: Rain Won't Stop You, Wind Won't Stop You: Live Music, Picture Books and Miyazawa Kenji in Two Languages
speakers.bio: Arthur is an American-born poet and translator who began writing poetry in Japanese after moving to Japan in 1990. His work spans poetry, essays, picture books, and kamishibai storytelling, including translations between Japanese and English.

speakers.name: Nick Szasz (FUKUOKA NOW)
speakers.session: Keynote 1: Why We Came, Why We Stayed, and What Comes Next
speakers.bio: Nick founded Fukuoka Now in 1998. Through English-language publishing, he introduces Fukuoka and Kyushu to international readers and helps connect visitors and residents with local places, people, and culture.

speakers.name: Douglas Weber
speakers.session: Keynote 1: Why We Came, Why We Stayed, and What Comes Next
speakers.bio: Douglas is a designer and engineer who studied at Stanford and worked on product design at Apple. At Weber Workshops, he brings that experience to the design and engineering of coffee equipment.

speakers.name: Jean-Pierre Villeneuve
speakers.session: Keynote 1: Why We Came, Why We Stayed, and What Comes Next
speakers.bio: Jean-Pierre is the founder and CEO of New Town Technologies, the company behind the Seratone karaoke system.
speakers.role: Founder and CEO, New Town Technologies

speakers.name: Micaela Anne
speakers.session: Keynote 1: Why We Came, Why We Stayed, and What Comes Next
speakers.bio: Micaela is a Canadian-born creator who calls Fukuoka home. Through Fukuoka Eats, she shares local food, travel, and everyday discoveries from the region.

speakers.name: Obaachan Shokudo
speakers.session: Gut-Health Breakfast: Elevating IQ and Happiness through Gut Health
speakers.bio: Ukiha no Takara is a social enterprise in Ukiha, Fukuoka. Its Grandma’s Café initiative creates meaningful paid work for older women, allowing them to share a lifetime of cooking skills, local recipes, hospitality, and wisdom. The team brings generations together through food, community, and a sense of purpose. At the Academy breakfast, the grandmothers share handmade onigiri and Japanese home cooking.

speakers.session: Gut-Health Breakfast: Elevating IQ and Happiness through Gut Health

The team brings generations together through food, community, and a sense of purpose. At the Academy breakfast, the grandmothers share handmade onigiri and Japanese home cooking.

speakers.name: Jacquie Wortley
speakers.session: Where can we build something that matters?
speakers.bio: Jacquie draws on a decade of UX and product research in her work on sustainable innovation. Working with rural tea farmers, she explores how projects can support local people and regenerate the places they depend on.

speakers.name: Ryu Fujii
speakers.session: Where can we build something that matters?
speakers.bio: Ryu co-founded 369meteor and co-organizes ZōVillage. He is involved with Fracton Ventures and Network School, connecting experimental global communities with grassroots initiatives.

speakers.name: MOE Nakano (JDNA)
speakers.session: Ask a Digital Nomad: Open Roundtables with JDNA
speakers.bio: Moe, also known as Tomoe Nakano, moved from design into community building through Asia’s coworking movement. She founded TAOHUB in Thailand, TANEHUB in Akita, and the Japan Digital Nomad Association, where she leads the Community Manager Academy.
speakers.role: Representative Director, Japan Digital Nomad Association

speakers.name: Vitto Christaldi (JDNA)
speakers.session: Ask a Digital Nomad: Open Roundtables with JDNA
speakers.bio: Vitto is a coworking and community strategist whose experience includes Hubud, Dojo, Tribal, and BWork. His work brings people together through shared workplaces and community experiences, including CU Asia.

speakers.name: Tessei Hosokawa
speakers.session: The "Death" of Digital Nomads — Zen, Impermanence, and Living in the Moment
speakers.bio: Tessei Hosokawa is a serial entrepreneur based in Kyoto, and the founder and CEO of NEWSON&COMPANY and Immersive Lab. As a university student, he spent six months in monastic training at Chōkokuji (Eiheiji Betsuin), a Sōtō Zen temple in Tokyo — rising before dawn for zazen, an experience that still shapes how he moves through a life of constant change. He later founded TABICA (now "aini"), one of Japan's early local-guide platforms connecting travelers with people and place. Through his companies he now works across community-building, regional revitalization, and immersive experiences. He serves as a director of the Japan Digital Nomad Association, an advisor to Japan's Digital Agency and the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, and is in his third year supporting the Japan Tourism Agency's digital nomad promotion program. As an advisor to the town of Nachikatsuura in Wakayama, he runs a nomad project hosted at a local Zen temple. In this session, he brings Zen's view of impermanence into dialogue with the modern nomadic life.

speakers.name: Akira Iguchi
speakers.session: IKIGAI MANIFESTATION: How to Turn Your Ikigai into an Extraordinary Life — The 5-Step Formula to Live the Life You Truly Want
speakers.bio:
Akira Iguchi  
Entrepreneur, Bestselling Author & International Speaker

Akira Iguchi is a Japanese entrepreneur, bestselling author, international speaker, and high-performance strategist dedicated to helping people reach their full potential and create extraordinary lives.

For more than two decades, Akira has studied and taught the principles of personal growth, entrepreneurship, high performance, and biohacking. As the founder of Human Plus Inc., he has built multimillion-dollar businesses and helped entrepreneurs and leaders transform their performance, businesses, health, and lives.

Akira is the author of 12 books, including the bestselling Lifestyle Millionaire, with more than 300,000 copies sold. He has spoken internationally across 12 countries and shared stages and events with some of the world’s most recognized entrepreneurs and thought leaders, including Richard Branson and Tony Robbins.

His work brings together business strategy, high performance, biohacking, and his signature Ikigai Manifestation Method, a framework designed to help people discover what they are uniquely meant to contribute, turn that potential into meaningful work, and create greater freedom, impact, and fulfillment.

Today, Akira works with entrepreneurs, founders, and high achievers around the world to help them elevate their health, wealth, performance, and purpose, while becoming the best version of themselves.

His mission is simple but ambitious:

Help 1 Billion People live their Ikigai and manifest all their dreams come true.

speakers.name: Jessica Hagmaier
speakers.bio: Jessica is a creative strategist, brand designer, and travel writer whose work explores reinvention and intentional living.
speakers.session: You Can't Outrun Your Life: How to Use Travel as a Catalyst for Reinvention

speakers.name: Christian Pedersen
speakers.session: Why Being Yourself Is Your Superpower
speakers.bio:
Christian is traveling the world making content that entertains and inspires millions of people, but it was not always like that.

He used to hate being in front of a camera, and had to make all the mistakes in the process of learning how to become the version of himself you see today.

Now he speaks and coaches on exactly that: how to get in front of a camera, be yourself, and really connect with people.
